subject.title: [Performance] Synchronous blocking on heavy plugin initialization delays startup

question: Should plugin services remain an ordered readiness barrier, or should the plugin service contract gain explicit dependency and abortable startup semantics so independent services can initialize concurrently?
rationale: Concurrency, timeout, quarantine, and late-completion handling change the public plugin lifecycle contract and cannot be selected safely from the report alone.

options.title: Instrument then design
options.body: Add service-level startup timing and use measured bottlenecks to design explicit dependency and cancellation semantics before enabling concurrency.

options.title: Keep ordered startup
options.body: Retain deterministic serial initialization and require plugins to make service start lightweight and move remote connection work into managed background tasks.

options.title: Adopt bounded concurrency
options.body: Extend the plugin API with dependency metadata and AbortSignal support, then concurrently start only services proven independent.

recommendation.title: Instrument then design
recommendation.body: Add service-level startup timing and use measured bottlenecks to design explicit dependency and cancellation semantics before enabling concurrency.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is the recent Gateway startup-sidecar performance and lifecycle work.
